raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add `vllm:kv_cache_blocks_by_state`, an opt-in per-engine gauge that splits the usable KV cache blocks (`num_gpu_blocks - 1`) into 9 exclusive states. `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` shows how full the cache is; this gauge shows what fills it: live work, stalled KV transfers, deferred frees, reclaimable prefix cache, or blocks with no owner.

## Claims

- New gauge `vllm:kv_cache_blocks_by_state{model_name, engine, state}` with states `active_shared`, `active_private`, `loading_kv`, `held_for_send`, `waiting_hold`, `pending_free`, `unattributed`, `cached_evictable`, `empty_free`. For one engine the series always sum to `num_gpu_blocks - 1`.
- Enabled by the existing `--kv-cache-metrics` flag (no new CLI flag or config field). With the flag off nothing changes: no count runs and the metric is not registered.
- Counted at most every 10 seconds while the engine is busy. When the engine goes idle after a busy count, it counts once more, and again only if the idle pool state changes (for example deferred frees drain). This stops the gauge from freezing at a busy value once `EngineCore.step` stops producing stats.
- Each count is one Python pass on the engine-core thread. Measured cost with real `KVCacheManager` objects: about 1 ms at 10k blocks, 5 ms at 50k blocks, and 17 to 21 ms at 200k blocks (see Validation).

## Validation

### Unit tests

New file `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_block_states.py` (`cpu_test`, picked up by the existing CPU step `pytest -v -s -m 'cpu_test' v1/core`; `check-test-tethering` passes). The tests use real `Scheduler` and `KVCacheManager` objects built by the existing test helpers. Every test checks that the counts sum to `num_gpu_blocks - 1`.

| Test | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `test_running_requests_split_shared_and_private` | Shared prefix blocks are `active_shared`, the rest `active_private` |
| `test_idle_after_busy_sample_is_emitted_once` | Going idle after a busy sample publishes even inside the 10 s window; the same idle state again, with no busy sample in between, is not recounted |
| `test_busy_sample_interval_ignores_idle_samples` | A burst that starts soon after an idle sample still gets a busy sample 10 s after the last busy sample; after that busy sample, going idle publishes again even though the idle state repeats the earlier one |
| `test_busy_samples_are_rate_limited` | Busy samples at t = 100 / 105 / 110 s: sample, no sample, sample |
| `test_deferred_frees_count_as_pending_free` | Real deferred-free gate (KV consumer, 2 batches in flight): deferred frees count as `pending_free`, not `unattributed`; after the drain a new idle sample is published |
| `test_remote_prefill_load_then_waiting_hold` | `loading_kv` while the async load runs, then `waiting_hold`, then `active_private` |
| `test_remote_decode_blocks_held_for_send` | P side: `held_for_send` until `finished_sending`, then cached free |
| `test_aborted_load_counts_as_held_for_send` | An aborted async load keeps its blocks as `held_for_send` until `finished_recving` |
| `test_external_pin_is_unattributed` | `BlockPool.touch` on a free cached block, as connectors and HiSparse do, gives `unattributed == 1` |
| `test_prometheus_gauge_per_engine[True/False]` | One child per engine and state; stats with no sample (`None`) leave the gauge unchanged; the metric is absent when the flag is off |

Mutation check: each rule was broken one at a time, and each break makes at least one new test fail:

| Mutation | Failing tests |
| --- | --- |
| Skip the `deferred_frees` walk | `test_deferred_frees_count_as_pending_free` |
| Never reset the idle key after a busy count | `test_busy_sample_interval_ignores_idle_samples` |
| Reset the idle key on every busy step (one count per request at concurrency 1) | `test_idle_after_busy_sample_is_emitted_once` |
| Idle counts also advance the busy timer | `test_busy_sample_interval_ignores_idle_samples` |
| Count finished requests as active | `test_remote_decode_blocks_held_for_send`, `test_aborted_load_counts_as_held_for_send` |
| No idle sample (time gate only) | `test_idle_after_busy_sample_is_emitted_once`, `test_busy_sample_interval_ignores_idle_samples`, `test_deferred_frees_count_as_pending_free` |
| Count a running load as `waiting_hold` | `test_remote_prefill_load_then_waiting_hold` |

Commands (CPU build of this branch, Python 3.12):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_block_states.py -v
# 11 passed
python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core
# 881 passed, 342 deselected
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_metrics.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py
# 30 passed
python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/kv_connector/unit
# 1081 passed, 3 skipped, 2141 deselected
python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/metrics
# 24 passed, 99 deselected
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
# all hooks passed (ruff, typos, markdownlint, mypy, SPDX, test tethering, config docstrings)
```

### Cost of one count

Measured with `count_kv_cache_blocks_by_state` on real `KVCacheManager` / `BlockPool` / `Request` objects: one full-attention group, prefix caching on, block size 16, 64 blocks per request, some requests sharing an 8-block prefix. The free pool was warmed so free blocks carry a hash. Median of 15 runs on a shared 64-core host (load average 5 to 9 during the run). Absolute numbers depend on the host.

| Blocks | Idle (all free, hashed) | Half (50% owned by running requests) | Full (about 100% owned) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10,000 | 1.0 ms | 1.2 ms | 1.3 ms |
| 50,000 | 4.4 ms | 5.1 ms | 5.6 ms |
| 200,000 | 17.3 ms | 19.6 ms | 20.5 ms |

Counts per engine: at most one every 10 seconds while busy, plus at most one each time the engine goes idle after a busy count (and one more if deferred frees drain while idle). With bursty traffic this means at most about two counts per 10 seconds, so for typical GPU pools (10k to 60k blocks) the average overhead is well under 0.1% of engine-loop time. The step that runs the count is still delayed by the amount above.

**Not run: GPU serving benchmark.** No GPU was available on the local CPU-only development machine to run `vllm bench serve` with and without `--kv-cache-metrics`; the classifier cost and end-to-end `Scheduler` -> `SchedulerStats` -> `PrometheusStatLogger.record()` -> `/metrics` pipeline were validated on CPU above.

## Details

### Where the count comes from

`Scheduler.make_stats` calls `_maybe_count_kv_cache_blocks_by_state()`, which calls the pure function `count_kv_cache_blocks_by_state()` in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_metrics.py`. All inputs are state the scheduler already keeps for its own correctness: `self.requests`, each single-type manager's `req_to_blocks`, `finished_recving_kv_req_ids`, `deferred_frees`, and the block pool. No new bookkeeping is added on any hot path.

Classification for each block (null block excluded):

1. Blocks in `req_to_blocks` of a request in `self.requests`, by request status:
   - `RUNNING`: `active_shared` if `ref_cnt > 1`, else `active_private`.
   - `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and the load has not finished: `loading_kv`.
   - Finished (the request stays in `self.requests` only while its free is delayed by a KV or EC connector): `held_for_send`.
   - Any other unfinished status (waiting or preempted while holding blocks, or the load finished but the request is not scheduled yet): `waiting_hold`.
2. Blocks in `deferred_frees` that are not already marked: `pending_free`.
3. A block with several owners takes the first matching state in the order above.
4. `unattributed` = in-use blocks minus marked blocks. `cached_evictable` = free blocks with a hash. `empty_free` = the other free blocks.

The marks go into a `bytearray` indexed by block id, so a block shared by several requests is counted once. The marked counts use `bytearray.count`, which runs in C. The only full pass over all blocks is the count of free blocks that have a hash. `BlockPool` keeps no O(1) count of those.

### Design decisions

- **9 states, not 8.** `pending_free` covers blocks in `deferred_frees` (KV consumer with async scheduling or pipeline parallelism). Their request is already deleted from `self.requests`, so without this state those blocks would show up as `unattributed` on every such P/D decode node.
- **`unattributed`, not "leak".** Copy-on-write, HiSparse, and some connectors (Mooncake store, UMBP) hold block references outside any request on purpose. The metric documentation says `unattributed` is not necessarily a leak. A value that stays non-zero on an idle engine without those features does point to leaked blocks.
- **Aborted async loads count as `held_for_send`.** After an abort, the status `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` is overwritten with `FINISHED_ABORTED`, and nothing else separates "aborted load" from "send in flight". The docs for `held_for_send` therefore say "free waits for a connector transfer (a KV send or store, an aborted async KV load, or an EC connector transfer)". If reviewers want them split, tracking the aborted request IDs in a set costs about 4 lines in `finish_requests` and `_free_blocks`.
- **Idle sample.** `EngineCore.step` returns no stats once `has_requests()` is false, so a periodic gauge would freeze at its last busy value. When the scheduler is idle it counts whenever `(num_free_blocks, len(deferred_frees))` differs from the last idle count. That check is O(1). A one-sample-per-idle-period flag would not be enough: under async scheduling a queued batch can drain `deferred_frees` after the engine goes idle. The idle key is cleared only when a busy count is published, so the gauge never stays at a busy value once idle, and idle counts are not repeated per request at low concurrency. Idle counts do not advance the 10 s busy timer, so a burst that starts soon after an idle count still gets its busy count on time. Trade-off: if the engine goes idle again in the same `(num_free_blocks, len(deferred_frees))` state with no busy count in between, it is not recounted, so the `cached_evictable` / `empty_free` split can lag; the in-use states are still right.
- **Why a snapshot, not O(1) counters.** Counters in `BlockPool` would need updates in `allocate_slots`, `free_blocks`, `touch`, eviction, `unpin_blocks`, deferred frees, and every request status change. That touches the hot path for every user to serve an opt-in metric, and any missed transition would drift silently. The snapshot reads existing state only, costs nothing when the flag is off, and is right by construction (the sum check is built in).
- **Opt-in.** The count is O(blocks) Python on the engine-core thread, so it is gated on `--kv-cache-metrics`, the existing opt-in flag for KV cache residency metrics (HiSparse host-pool histograms also use it). The 10 s interval is a module constant (`KV_CACHE_BLOCK_STATES_INTERVAL_S`). I did not add a config field without a demonstrated need.
- **Transport.** New field `SchedulerStats.kv_cache_blocks_by_state: dict[str, int] | None = None`. `None` means "no new sample", so the bare `SchedulerStats` objects published for DP load balancing do not overwrite the gauge. The frontend sets the children only when the field is not `None`. The gauge uses `multiprocess_mode="mostrecent"` like the other scheduler gauges.
- **Scope.** Only the main device pool is counted. HiSparse host-pool blocks are skipped; host occupancy already has HiSparse metrics. Hybrid models share one pool, so all KV cache groups merge into one count. DP engines are separated by the `engine` label.
- **Name.** `vllm:kv_cache_blocks_by_state`. Some upstream count gauges use the `num_*_by_*` form (`vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage`). I can rename to `vllm:num_kv_cache_blocks_by_state` if reviewers prefer.

### Known limitations

- Before the first request, all series read 0.
- `reset_prefix_cache` or sleep-mode calls on an idle engine produce no stats, so `cached_evictable` stays stale until the next step.
- The full-pass cost grows with pool size (about 20 ms at 200k blocks on this host). If that matters for large pools, the hashed-free count can walk the free queue instead of all blocks.

### Docs

- `vllm/config/observability.py`: the `kv_cache_metrics` docstring, which also feeds `--help`, now mentions the gauge.
- `docs/design/metrics.md`: new "KV Cache Block States" section.
- `docs/usage/metrics.md` is generated from `loggers.py`, so the gauge and its `documentation=` text appear there automatically.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed PRs (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search` for "kv cache blocks by state", "kv_cache_blocks_by_state", and "kv cache block state metric"): no PR adds a per-state block breakdown. The nearest open PRs complement this one: #54183 exports KV cache capacity in bytes, and #57336 adds `vllm:kv_cache_token_usage_perc`.

### AI assistance

AI assistance (Gemini) was used to research, implement, and test this change. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by:` trailer and a DCO `Signed-off-by:`.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- The full-pass cost grows with pool size (about 20 ms at 200k blocks on this host). If that matters for large pools, the hashed-free count can walk the free queue instead of all blocks.

### Docs

- `vllm/config/observability.py`: the `kv_cache_metrics` docstring, which also feeds `--help`, now mentions the gauge.
- `docs/design/metrics.md`: new "KV Cache Block States" section.
- `docs/usage/metrics.md` is generated from `loggers.py`, so the gauge and its `documentation=` text appear there automatically.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed PRs (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search` for "kv cache blocks by state", "kv_cache_blocks_by_state", and "kv cache block state metric"): no PR adds a per-state block breakdown. The nearest open PRs complement this one: #54183 exports KV cache capacity in bytes, and #57336 adds `vllm:kv_cache_token_usage_perc`.

@@ -293,6 +293,41 @@ exposes the same data through `LLM.get_metrics()` when logging is on.
 Looking at lifetime and idle time on one chart makes it easy to spot
 stranded cache or workloads that pin prompts for a long decode.
 
+### KV Cache Block States
+
+`--kv-cache-metrics` also enables the `vllm:kv_cache_blocks_by_state`
+gauge. The scheduler splits the usable blocks of each engine
+(`num_gpu_blocks - 1`, the null block is excluded) into exclusive states,
+so the series of one engine always sum to that number:
+
+- `active_shared` / `active_private` – owned by a running request,
+  with `ref_cnt > 1` (shared with another request, a deferred free,
+  copy-on-write, or an external pin) / `ref_cnt == 1`.
+- `loading_kv` – owned by a request whose async KV load is in progress.
+- `held_for_send` – owned by a finished request whose free waits for a
+  connector transfer (a KV send or store, an aborted async KV load, or an
+  EC connector transfer).
+- `waiting_hold` – owned by a waiting or preempted request.
+- `pending_free` – freed, but withheld until an in-flight step completes
+  (deferred block freeing with async scheduling or pipeline parallelism).
+- `unattributed` – in use without an owner request or a deferred free.
+- `cached_evictable` / `empty_free` – free, with / without a prefix-cache
+  hash.
+
+A block owned by several requests takes the first matching state in the
+list above. `unattributed` is not necessarily a leak: copy-on-write,
+HiSparse, and some connectors (for example Mooncake store) pin blocks
+outside any request. A persistent non-zero value on an idle engine without
+such features does indicate leaked blocks.
+
+The count is one pass over the blocks on the engine core thread, so it
+runs at most every 10 seconds while busy. When the engine goes idle after a
+busy count, it counts again so the gauge does not freeze at a busy value,
+and again whenever the idle pool state changes (for example when deferred
+frees drain). A repeated idle state with no busy count in between is not
+recounted, so the `cached_evictable` / `empty_free` split may lag after
+short bursts; the in-use states stay correct.
+
 ### Metrics Publishing - Logging
 
 The `LoggingStatLogger` metrics publisher outputs a log `INFO` message

+"""Tests for the `vllm:kv_cache_blocks_by_state` block counts."""

+NUM_BLOCKS = 100
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+# 2 full blocks and 1 partial block.
+NUM_PROMPT_TOKENS = 2 * BLOCK_SIZE + 8

+
+def _expected(**counts: int) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """All states, with `empty_free` holding the remaining blocks."""
+    expected = dict.fromkeys(KV_CACHE_BLOCK_STATES, 0)
+    expected.update(counts)
+    expected["empty_free"] = NUM_BLOCKS - 1 - sum(counts.values())
+    return expected
+
+
+def _count(scheduler) -> dict[str, int]:
+    counts = count_kv_cache_blocks_by_state(
+        scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool,
+        scheduler.kv_cache_manager.coordinator.single_type_managers,
+        scheduler.requests,
+        scheduler.finished_recving_kv_req_ids,
+        scheduler.deferred_frees,
+    )
+    assert sum(counts.values()) == NUM_BLOCKS - 1
+    return counts
+
+
+def _stats_counts(engine_core_outputs) -> dict[str, int] | None:
+    stats = next(iter(engine_core_outputs.values())).scheduler_stats
+    counts = stats.kv_cache_blocks_by_state
+    if counts is not None:
+        assert sum(counts.values()) == NUM_BLOCKS - 1
+    return counts
+
+
+def _step(scheduler, requests, token_id: int = 0):
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    return scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduler_output,
+        create_model_runner_output(reqs=requests, token_id=token_id),

+
+
+def test_running_requests_split_shared_and_private():
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(enable_prefix_caching=True, num_blocks=NUM_BLOCKS)

+        num_requests=2, num_tokens=NUM_PROMPT_TOKENS, same_prompt=True
+    )

+    scheduler.add_request(second)

+    (request,) = create_requests(

+    cached_block = next(b for b in block_pool.blocks if b.block_hash is not None)

+def test_hisparse_unpinned_blocks_and_residency_changes():
+    """Unpinned (`ref_cnt == 0`) blocks on `free_block_queue` count as free,

+    """

+    assert isinstance(resident_manager, HiSparseResidentManager)
+    block_pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool

+    request.status = RequestStatus.RUNNING
+    scheduler.requests[request.request_id] = request
+    resident_manager.allocate_external_computed_blocks(

+        num_external_computed_tokens=BLOCK_SIZE,

+    tail_block = resident_manager.req_to_blocks[request.request_id][1]

+    assert _count(scheduler) == _expected(active_private=1)

+def count_kv_cache_blocks_by_state(
+    block_pool: "BlockPool",
+    managers: Sequence["SingleTypeKVCacheManager"],
+    requests: Mapping[str, Request],
+    finished_recving_req_ids: Container[str],
+    deferred_frees: Iterable[tuple[int, Sequence["KVCacheBlock"]]],
+) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """Count the usable blocks of a pool by exclusive state.
+
+    Every block except the null block gets exactly one state, so the counts
+    sum to `block_pool.num_gpu_blocks - 1`. A block owned by several
+    requests takes the highest-priority state, in the order of
+    `KV_CACHE_BLOCK_STATES`. In-use blocks without an owner request or a
+    deferred free (e.g. connector or copy-on-write pins) are `unattributed`.
+
+    Args:
+        block_pool: The pool to count. Blocks of other pools are skipped.
+        managers: Single-type managers whose `req_to_blocks` own blocks.
+        requests: Scheduler requests by ID.
+        finished_recving_req_ids: Requests whose async KV load finished.
+        deferred_frees: `(step_id, blocks)` pairs withheld from the pool until
+            the step finishes.
+
+    Returns:
+        Block count for every state in `KV_CACHE_BLOCK_STATES`.
+
+    """
+    marks = bytearray(block_pool.num_gpu_blocks)
+    for manager in managers:
+        if manager.block_pool is not block_pool:
+            continue
+        residency_changes = getattr(manager, "residency_changes", None)
+        for req_id, blocks in manager.req_to_blocks.items():
+            request = requests.get(req_id)
+            if request is None:
